text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Moslem-Croat federation parliament's House of Representatives adopts a law on 1997 budget, its execution law and the law on sale of the apartments with existing tenancy rights. The laws need to be adopted by the parliament's upper House of People.

- Croat deputies in the federation parliament did not attend Wednesday's session because the Moslem deputies refused to accept a Croat proposal to reconsider legislation on new municipalities which was adopted at the previous session, newspaper says.
- Bosnia's three man presidency discussed the Sintra meeting conclusions and agreed on the basic guidelines for attending a donors' fund-raising conference on June 24 and 25.
- Bosnian Insurance Bureau is to become an official member of European Insurance Bureau by July 1.
- Association of Bosnian Journalists demands return of confiscated satirical paper Polikita seized by the federation police on Saturday for its mocking of politicians.
- Major of Brcko in exile Munib Jusufovic says closing of four voter registration centres in town is a step forward in building confidence in the OSCE.

- If the donors' conference does not take place for all of Bosnia and with the presence of Serb republic, the influence of the international community in Bosnia will be futile, says Zlatko Lagumdzija, leader of the Social Democratic Party.
- Chairman of Bosnian presidency Alija Izetbegovic and Croatian President Franjo Tudjman might meet on June 23 in Split, daily quotes government sources. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387 71 663 864
